key_insight: WorldDirector separates motion control from pixel generation, making video world models more controllable and able to remember dynamic objects persistently. This enables longer-horizon scene simulation and free viewpoint exploration without depending on continuous visual input.
problem_solved: Existing world models often mix physical dynamics with rendering, which makes control difficult and causes motion to fade when visual observations are absent. This paper addresses the need for a world simulator that can maintain object state over time while allowing flexible camera and trajectory control.
method: Use an LLM to orchestrate semantic motion, including 3D trajectories and camera movements.
Decouple dynamic reasoning from visual synthesis so object behavior can persist independently of pixel generation.
Generate world-consistent video from structured motion plans, supporting unrestricted viewpoint exploration.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more controllable way to build video-based simulators for robotics, gaming, and embodied AI. It can improve long-horizon consistency, editability, and user-directed scene simulation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing LLM motion planning separate from video rendering

Timeline illustrating persistent object memory across frames
Camera-path and 3D trajectory overlay on a simulated scene
paper_title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
paper_authors: Hanlin Wang, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Wen Wang, Qingyan Bai
